root_cause.text: During sound card unbind, the delayed work flush occurs before snd_card_disconnect_sync() can trigger new delayed work via PCM close, leaving that scheduled work to fire after DAPM widgets have been freed, causing a use-after-free in snd_soc_dapm_stream_event().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "During unbind, snd_soc_unbind_card() flushes delayed work and then calls soc_cleanup_card_resources(). Inside cleanup, snd_card_disconnect_sync() releases all PCM file descriptors, and the resulting PCM close path can call snd_soc_dapm_stream_stop() which schedules new delayed work with a pmdown_time timer delay. Since this happens after the flush in snd_soc_unbind_card(), the new work is not caught. soc_remove_link_components() then frees DAPM widgets before this work fires, leading to the use-after-free." The patch adds a second flush after snd_card_disconnect_sync() to ensure no new delayed work remains before removing DAIs and widgets.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over each rtd, and its execution after potential delayed work scheduling but before a proper disconnect sync can lead to operations on freed widgets.
This conditional check gates the link exit; if delayed work is pending, this check does not prevent the subsequent removal from causing a use-after-free.
This call tears down the link, potentially freeing structures that delayed work may still access, because the work cancellation/flush was not performed beforehand.
Removing DAIs is a critical step that frees DAPM widgets and other resources; executing this without ensuring all delayed work is cancelled leads to use-after-free.
Removing components finalizes the teardown; any delayed work that was scheduled after a flush but before disconnect sync will now fire on freed memory.

    Flows leading to link->init() and link->exit() are not symmetric.
    Currently the relevant part of card probe sequence goes as:
    
            for_each_card_rtds(card, rtd)

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit moves snd_soc_link_exit() from snd_soc_remove_pcm_runtime() to soc_cleanup_card_resources(), executing it before soc_remove_link_dais() and soc_remove_link_components(). This ensures that link exit (rtd->exit()) happens before component removal, preventing the use-after-free that occurs when link->exit() accesses freed component resources. In the resulting code, the vulnerable ordering is eliminated and the fix is present.
